events.title: Coronation of Elizabeth I
events.description: Elizabeth I was crowned Queen of England at Westminster Abbey in London, in a ceremony led by Owen Oglethorpe, Bishop of Carlisle, after the death of her half-sister Mary I.
events.significance: Her 44-year reign ushered in the Elizabethan era, establishing the Church of England's Protestant settlement, defeating the Spanish Armada in 1588, and fostering a flourishing of English arts and exploration.

events.title: British Museum Opens
events.description: The British Museum opened to the public for the first time in Montagu House in Bloomsbury, London, based on the collections of physician and naturalist Sir Hans Sloane.
events.significance: It became the world's first national public museum covering all fields of human knowledge, and it set a model for public access to cultural and scientific heritage.

events.title: Birth of Martin Luther King Jr.
events.description: Martin Luther King Jr. was born in Atlanta, Georgia. He became a Baptist minister and the foremost leader of the American civil rights movement, advocating nonviolent resistance.
events.significance: King's leadership in events such as the Montgomery Bus Boycott and the March on Washington helped bring about the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965. His birthday is a US federal holiday.

events.title: Wikipedia Launched
events.description: Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger launched Wikipedia, a free online encyclopedia written collaboratively by volunteers.
events.significance: Wikipedia grew into one of the most visited websites in the world and transformed how people access and share knowledge, demonstrating the power of open collaborative editing.

events.title: Great Molasses Flood in Boston
events.description: A large storage tank containing over two million gallons of molasses burst in Boston's North End, sending a wave through the streets that killed 21 people and injured about 150.
events.significance: The disaster led to stricter regulations on construction and engineering oversight in the United States, including requirements for engineers to certify structural plans, and it became a landmark case in class-action litigation.
